Prevention: Remove host plants around bunds and surrounding areas such as crabgrass, goose grass and beans.
Preserve beneficial insects (such as wasps, spiders) by spraying less insecticides at early growth stage (first 30 days).
Monitoring: Causes the most damage during milking stage.
Scout on alternate day from pre-flowering to dough stage.
Use mosquito net in the early morning or late afternoon to catch and monitor.
Randomly scout 20 hills, consider treatment if 10 or more bugs found per hill, or over 3 bugs per square meter.
Direct Control: Spray aromatic soap solution to expel the rice bug (e.g. lemon grass solution).
Use ‘prahok’ (local cheese) near the field to attract, trap and kill the rice bug.
Use a mosquito net to catch the rice bugs.
After that crush them and mix in water and spray onto plants to repel other rice bugs.
Restrictions: Spray in morning between 6-10 am or in afternoon between 3-6 pm
Killing natural enemies could lead to outbreaks of secondary pests
